content: In 2017, a meeting was held where a researcher reported on a WHO/TDR research grant. This grant focused on studying the extent and causes of residual malaria transmission in Thailand and Vietnam, with the project being completed in 2018. The researcher also outlined plans to investigate the impact of socio-ecological systems and resilience (SESR)-based strategies on controlling dengue vectors in schools and neighboring household communities in Cambodia. As of November 2017, this study was awaiting ethical approval. The Guidelines Development Group (GDG) for 2021 included the following members: Dr. Dorothy Achu, Program Manager of the National Malaria Control Programme in Yaoundé, Cameroon. Prof. Basil Brooke, Associate Professor at the University of Witwatersrand and the National Institute for Communicable Diseases in Johannesburg, South Africa. Prof. Ahmad Ali Enayati, Head of the Medical Entomology Department at Mazandaran University of Medical Sciences in Sari, Iran. Ms. Mihiri Hewavitharane, Entomology Technical Manager for the PMI VectorLink Project in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. Dr. Seth Irish, Research Entomologist at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention in Atlanta, USA. Prof. Fang Jing, Director of the Institute for Health Sciences at Kunming Medical University in Yunnan Province, China. Dr. Keziah Malm, Program Manager of the National Malaria Control Programme in Accra, Ghana. Dr. Kui Muraya, Social Scientist at the KEMRI-Wellcome Trust in Nairobi, Kenya. Prof. Martha Quiñones, Professor at Universidad Nacional de Colombia in Bogotá, Colombia. Dr. Christina Rundi, Health Director at the Sabah Health Department, Ministry of Health, Malaysia. Dr. Tanya Russell, Research Fellow at James Cook University in Cairns, Australia. Dr. Lucy Tusting, Assistant Professor at the Faculty of Infectious Tropical Diseases, London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine (LSHTM), UK. Dr. Josh Yukich, Associate Professor in the Department of Tropical Medicine at Tulane University School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine in New Orleans, USA. The GDG for 2022 and 2023 included many of the same members, with additional experts such as Dr. Charles Wondji from the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine and the Centre for Research in Infectious Diseases in Cameroon. The Guidelines Steering Group (2021–2023) included: Dr. Samira Al-Eryani from the WHO Regional Office for the Eastern Mediterranean in Cairo, Egypt. Dr. Haroldo Bezerra from the WHO Regional Office for the Americas in Washington, D.C., USA. Dr. Maurice Bucagu from the Family, Women, Children, and Adolescents division at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Emmanuel Chanda from the WHO Regional Office for Africa in Brazzaville, Congo. Dr. Florence Fouque from the Special Programme for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Riffat Hossain from the Programme for Health and Migration at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Tessa Knox from the WHO Country Office in Vanuatu. Dr. Jan Kolaczinski from the Global Malaria Programme at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. Mrs. Marion Law from the Prequalification Team for Vector Control at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Kim Lindblade from the Global Malaria Programme at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Katherine Littler from the Department of Research for Health at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Ramona Ludolph from the Environment, Climate Change, and Health division at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Edith Patouillard from the Global Malaria Programme at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Matt Shortus from the WHO Country Office in Lao PDR. Dr. Jennifer Stevenson from the Global Malaria Programme at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Raman Velayudhan from the Department of Control of Neglected Tropical Diseases at WHO in Geneva, Switzerland. The External Review Group (ERG) for 2021 and 2022 included: Dr. Jenifer Armistead from the Malaria Division at USAID in the USA. Prof. Maureen Coetzee from the University of the Witwatersrand in South Africa. Prof. Umberto d’Alessandro, Director of the Medical Research Council Unit in Gambia. Dr. Scott Filler from the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria in Geneva, Switzerland. Dr. Caroline Jones, Senior Social Scientist at the KEMRI Wellcome Trust Research Programme in Kenya. Prof. Neil Lobo from the University of Notre Dame in the USA. Dr. Lucy Tusting declared receiving research funding exceeding £5000 in the last four years for studies on the impact of housing improvements on malaria, funded by the UK Medical Research Council. She was the principal investigator of this study, which supported 100% of her income through 2022. She also held unpaid roles related to housing and malaria, receiving travel expenses for these activities. Dr. Tusting worked on a project in Uganda funded by the NIH, analyzing data on the relationship between housing and malaria. She co-directed the BOVA network (Building Out Vector-Borne Diseases in Africa) since 2017, focusing on preventing diseases like malaria, dengue, and Zika through built environment improvements. From 2017 to 2020, she co-chaired the RBM VCWG’s workstream on vector-borne diseases and the built environment. She led key reviews on housing type and its impact on malaria, including systematic reviews and meta-analyses published in Malaria Journal and PLOS Medicine. Dr. Umberto d’Alessandro reported receiving research funding exceeding $5000 in the last four years for projects on improved housing and malaria elimination strategies in sub-Saharan Africa. Dr. Jenifer Armistead reported involvement in projects funded by PMI, including monitoring PBO synergist ITNs in Nigeria and assessing housing modifications combined with PBO LLINs in Uganda. Prof. Maureen Coetzee supervised a PhD project investigating spatial information tools for targeted urban planning interventions to control malaria and lymphatic filariasis in Tanzania.
